input: Book a professional voice lesson for beginners

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who the lesson is for (the user themselves, a child, a gift for someone else) changes the type of teacher, scheduling, and communication needed.
Voice lessons can focus on singing (classical, pop, musical theatre, etc.) or speaking (public speaking, vocal coaching) — the goal completely changes which teacher to look for.
Whether lessons happen in-person or online determines which geographic area to search, platform logistics, and available teacher pools.
Budget per lesson directly filters the range of teachers and lesson lengths that are realistic to book.
Availability (days of the week, time of day) is a hard scheduling constraint that must match the teacher's openings.
Teacher preferences such as gender, teaching style, or experience with a specific genre can affect comfort and learning outcomes, especially for a beginner.
Understanding whether the user wants a one-off trial lesson or an ongoing series determines how to structure the booking and what commitment to look for.

gold.taskTitle: Book a beginner professional voice lesson
gold.taskDescription: Find and book a professional voice lesson suited for a beginner singer or speaker.

questions.title: Who is this voice lesson actually for?
questions.description: Determine whether the lesson is for the user themselves, a child, or as a gift for someone else, as this affects teacher type and communication.

questions.title: Should the focus be singing or spoken voice?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is singing (and in what genre, e.g. pop, classical) or spoken voice coaching (e.g. public speaking, accent work), as this defines the teacher specialty needed.

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person lessons or online ones?
questions.description: Establish whether the lesson format should be in-person (requiring a local teacher) or online (opening up a wider pool of teachers via video platforms).

questions.title: What is your budget per lesson session?
questions.description: Determine a comfortable price range per lesson to filter teachers and session lengths that are financially viable.

questions.title: Which days and times are you generally available?
questions.description: Identify scheduling availability to narrow down teachers whose open slots actually match, avoiding wasted outreach.

questions.title: Do you have any preferences for the teacher's style or background?
questions.description: Understand if the user has preferences around teaching approach, teacher gender, experience level, or specific genre expertise to ensure a good fit.

questions.title: Are you looking for one trial lesson or a recurring series?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a single introductory session to test it out, or wants to commit to a regular schedule of lessons from the start.
